topics.label: Core Web Vitals
topics.desc: Google's user-centric performance metrics, LCP for loading, INP for interactivity, and CLS for visual stability, that feed real-world UX scoring and search ranking signals.

topics.label: Largest Contentful Paint
topics.desc: A Core Web Vital measuring when the largest visible element finishes rendering, with a good target under 2.5 seconds at the 75th percentile of real users.

topics.label: Interaction to Next Paint
topics.desc: The Core Web Vital that replaced FID, measuring overall responsiveness as the worst latency from a user interaction to the next visual update, ideally under 200ms.

topics.label: Cumulative Layout Shift
topics.desc: A Core Web Vital scoring unexpected layout movement during load, where a good value stays under 0.1, fixed by reserving space for images, ads, and fonts.

topics.label: TTFB & FCP
topics.desc: Early loading milestones: Time to First Byte marks when the response starts arriving, and First Contentful Paint marks when the user first sees any text or image.

topics.label: Lighthouse
topics.desc: Google's open-source auditing tool, built into Chrome DevTools and PageSpeed Insights, that scores performance, accessibility, SEO, and best practices with actionable diagnostics.

topics.label: Performance Budgets
topics.desc: Enforced limits on metrics like bundle size, request count, or LCP that fail CI when exceeded, keeping performance from regressing as features ship over time.

topics.label: RUM vs Synthetic
topics.desc: Field measurement via real-user monitoring (CrUX, web-vitals.js, the Performance API's performance.now and PerformanceObserver) versus synthetic lab tests in WebPageTest or Lighthouse CI.

topics.label: Code Splitting
topics.desc: Breaking a bundle into smaller chunks loaded on demand via dynamic import() or route boundaries, so the browser downloads only the JavaScript a view actually needs.

topics.label: Lazy Loading
topics.desc: Deferring the fetch of components, images, or routes until needed or near the viewport, via React.lazy, dynamic imports, or loading="lazy" on media elements.

topics.label: Bundle Optimization
topics.desc: Shrinking shipped JavaScript via tree-shaking unused exports, analyzing bundles with webpack-bundle-analyzer, minification, and gzip/brotli compression to cut download bytes.

topics.label: Image Optimization
topics.desc: Shrinking image payloads with modern formats like WebP and AVIF, responsive srcset/sizes, correct dimensions, and lazy loading, since images are usually the heaviest asset.

topics.label: Critical CSS & Fonts
topics.desc: Cutting render-blocking work by inlining above-the-fold critical CSS and optimizing web fonts via woff2, subsetting, and font-display: swap to speed first paint and avoid FOIT.

topics.label: Resource Hints
topics.desc: Markup hints (preload, prefetch, preconnect, dns-prefetch) that tell the browser to fetch critical assets early or warm connections to origins it will soon need.

topics.label: Render Optimization
topics.desc: Reducing runtime UI work by debouncing and throttling noisy events, memoizing expensive renders with React.memo/useMemo, and virtualizing long lists with react-window.

topics.label: Response-Time Optimization
topics.desc: Reducing server latency by trimming slow code paths, cutting redundant work, parallelizing I/O, and adding caching, measured at the p50, p95, and p99 percentiles.

topics.label: Query Optimization
topics.desc: Speeding up database access with proper indexes, EXPLAIN/EXPLAIN ANALYZE plans, selecting only needed columns, and avoiding full table scans on hot paths.

topics.label: N+1 Problem
topics.desc: A common ORM pitfall where fetching a list then querying per row causes N extra round trips, fixed by eager loading, joins, or DataLoader-style batching.

topics.label: Connection Pooling
topics.desc: Reusing a bounded set of open database connections instead of opening one per request, via poolers like PgBouncer or built-in drivers, to avoid handshake overhead.

topics.label: Pagination
topics.desc: Returning large result sets in bounded pages using offset/limit or faster cursor (keyset) pagination, protecting memory, response time, and the database from huge scans.

topics.label: Async & Non-Blocking
topics.desc: Handling I/O without blocking threads using async/await, event loops, or coroutines, so a server can serve many concurrent requests while waiting on network and disk.

topics.label: Profiling Hotspots
topics.desc: Measuring where server time and memory actually go using flame graphs, CPU profilers, and APM traces to target the true bottlenecks instead of guessing.

topics.label: Browser Cache
topics.desc: The browser's local store of fetched assets keyed by URL, reused on later visits per HTTP cache headers to avoid re-downloading unchanged files entirely.

topics.label: HTTP Caching
topics.desc: Controlling reuse of responses with Cache-Control, Expires, ETag/Last-Modified validators, and stale-while-revalidate, letting browsers and proxies skip or revalidate fetches.

topics.label: CDN Caching
topics.desc: Serving cacheable content from edge nodes near users via Cloudflare, Fastly, or CloudFront to slash latency and offload origin servers through geographically distributed PoPs.

topics.label: Server-Side Caching
topics.desc: Storing computed results, rendered pages, or query output on the server to avoid recomputation, spanning in-process memory, shared stores, and full-page or fragment caches.

topics.label: Redis & In-Memory Cache
topics.desc: Using fast in-memory key-value stores like Redis or Memcached as a shared cache layer with TTLs, holding sessions, query results, and hot data near the application.

topics.label: Caching Patterns
topics.desc: Strategies for reading and writing through a cache, including cache-aside (lazy loading), write-through, write-behind, and read-through, each trading consistency for speed.

topics.label: Cache Invalidation
topics.desc: Keeping cached data fresh by expiring or purging stale entries via TTLs, event-based busting, or versioned keys; famously one of the hard problems in computing.

topics.label: Horizontal vs Vertical
topics.desc: The two ways to add capacity: scaling up with a bigger machine (vertical) versus scaling out with more instances behind a balancer (horizontal), the basis of elastic systems.

topics.label: Load Balancing
topics.desc: Distributing incoming traffic across instances with algorithms like round-robin or least-connections, plus health checks, via Nginx, HAProxy, or cloud L4/L7 balancers.

topics.label: Rate Limiting
topics.desc: Capping how many requests a client may make in a window using token-bucket or sliding-window algorithms to protect capacity, prevent abuse, and ensure fairness.

topics.label: Queues & Backpressure
topics.desc: Buffering work in message queues like SQS, RabbitMQ, or Kafka to smooth spikes, and applying backpressure to slow producers when consumers fall behind, preventing overload.

topics.label: Autoscaling
topics.desc: Automatically adding or removing instances based on metrics like CPU, request rate, or queue depth, via Kubernetes HPA or cloud groups, to match capacity to demand.

topics.label: Statelessness for Scale
topics.desc: Keeping app servers free of local session state so any instance can serve any request, pushing state to shared stores, a prerequisite for clean horizontal scaling.

topics.label: Load Testing
topics.desc: Simulating concurrent traffic to find breaking points and capacity limits using tools like k6, Locust, JMeter, or Gatling, including stress, soak, and spike tests.

topics.label: Observability vs Monitoring
topics.desc: Monitoring watches known dashboards and alerts for expected failures, while observability, via metrics, logs, and traces, lets you ask new questions about unknown problems.

topics.label: Four Golden Signals
topics.desc: Google SRE's core service health metrics, latency, traffic, errors, and saturation, that give a compact, high-signal starting point for monitoring any system.

topics.label: Metrics & Dashboards
topics.desc: Collecting numeric time-series like request rate or memory with Prometheus and charting them on Grafana dashboards, or using hosted platforms such as Datadog and New Relic.

topics.label: APM
topics.desc: Application Performance Monitoring tools that auto-instrument code to surface slow endpoints, traces, and database calls, e.g. Datadog APM, New Relic, and Elastic APM.

topics.label: Uptime Monitoring
topics.desc: Periodically probing endpoints from outside via Pingdom, UptimeRobot, or Better Uptime to detect outages and measure availability, often driving public status pages.

topics.label: Alerting
topics.desc: Firing notifications when metrics cross thresholds, routed through Alertmanager, PagerDuty, or Opsgenie, while tuning rules to avoid noisy, fatigue-inducing false alarms.

topics.label: SLI, SLO & SLA
topics.desc: Reliability targets: SLIs measure behavior like success rate, SLOs set internal goals with error budgets, and SLAs are contractual promises with penalties to customers.

topics.label: Structured Logging
topics.desc: Emitting logs as machine-parseable key-value JSON rather than free text, so fields can be filtered, aggregated, and queried; produced by libraries like Pino, Winston, or Zap.

topics.label: Log Levels
topics.desc: Severity tiers, DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR, and FATAL, that classify log importance, letting you filter noise in production while keeping detail available when debugging.

topics.label: Log Aggregation
topics.desc: Shipping logs from many services into a central, searchable store such as the ELK/Elastic Stack, Grafana Loki, or Splunk, so you can query across the whole system.

topics.label: Correlation IDs
topics.desc: A unique request ID propagated through headers across services and attached to every log line, letting you stitch together one request's journey through a distributed system.

topics.label: Distributed Tracing
topics.desc: Following a single request as linked spans across services to see where time is spent, visualized in Jaeger, Zipkin, or Tempo to debug latency in microservices.

topics.label: OpenTelemetry
topics.desc: The vendor-neutral CNCF standard and SDKs for generating and exporting traces, metrics, and logs, letting you instrument once and send telemetry to any backend.

topics.label: Error Monitoring
topics.desc: Automatically capturing, reporting, and aggregating runtime exceptions with full stack traces and context using services like Sentry, Rollbar, Bugsnag, or Honeybadger.

topics.label: Production Source Maps
topics.desc: Uploading source maps to error trackers so minified frontend stack traces map back to original code with real file names and line numbers, without exposing source publicly.

topics.label: Error Grouping
topics.desc: Fingerprinting similar exceptions into a single issue with an occurrence count, so a flood of identical errors becomes one trackable, deduplicated item to triage.

topics.label: Error Alerting
topics.desc: Notifying the team when new or spiking errors appear, routed to Slack or PagerDuty with rules on volume or regression to surface real incidents without noise.

topics.label: Debugging Production
topics.desc: Diagnosing live incidents using error context, breadcrumbs, release tracking, logs, and traces, often correlating a spike to a specific deploy to find and roll back the cause.
